hero.title: The voice that returned after 30 years of silence

manifesto.eyebrow: From the Olympia to the walls of Jerusalem
manifesto.text: He once sang about love in French, under the name Gilbert. Then he fell silent for thirty years to study. Today the same voice sings in Hebrew, for joy and for faith.

items.title: The story
items.text: Gilbert Mathis, Gilbert Sitbon, then Aharon: a life no one would have dared to script.

items.title: The music
items.text: Two albums and more than twenty singles since 2014, all here, song by song.

items.title: On stage
items.text: From the Olympia in 1977 to Menorah Hall: the stages his voice has filled.

span.title: Fifty years, one voice
span.text: In 1977 he appears on French television and sings at the Olympia. Nearly fifty years later he sings before the walls of the Old City. In between: thirty years of silence, and a promise kept.

story.title: From Gilbert to Aharon
story.intro: The great turning points of a life in two acts, as the press has told them. The rest he tells best himself, on stage.

steps.title: A house full of music
steps.text: He grows up in a traditional family of eight children. His older sister sings and plays the oud; one of his brothers will become a drummer for the great names of French song.

steps.title: The guitar
steps.text: The family settles in France, first in Marseille, then Paris. At around seventeen, the guitar takes hold of him for good.

steps.title: The stage
steps.text: A contest won, a first single, tours. He is known as Gilbert Mathis, and later as Gilbert Sitbon. His agent, Rolande Bismuth, also looks after Yves Duteil and Michel Fugain.

steps.title: The Olympia
steps.text: He appears on Philippe Bouvard's TV show and sings six songs at the Olympia, opening for Herbert Pagani.

steps.title: Tefillin
steps.text: In Paris, Chabad Chassidim offer him to put on tefillin. It shakes him deeply. Little by little he leaves the stage, just as he is offered a long touring contract.

steps.title: Silence
steps.text: He studies Torah and earns his living in other ways. His children, then his grandchildren, have no idea he was ever a singer.

steps.title: The old guitar
steps.text: Settled in Israel, in Jerusalem, he takes out his old guitar. A melody by his friend Michel Fugain keeps him awake at night, and he sets the words of Adon Olam to it.

steps.title: Adon Olam
steps.text: Producer Youval Stoupel hears it and releases it as a single. Unsure about a comeback at his age, he opens the Lubavitcher Rebbe's letters and reads that an artist who returns to faith should place his talent in the service of holiness. He has his answer.

steps.title: Two albums
steps.text: “Shehecheyanu”, whose proceeds went to the Eshel Tsion charity, then “Higia Zman Geulatchem”, three years in the making with Eli Klein and Yitzy Berry.

steps.title: More songs
steps.text: “Or Be'einai”, a melody he was already singing in 1977, “Odeh Hashem Elokai” during the war, “Tefila LeShalom”, then “Niggun Yehudi” for Purim. His mission: to bring joy to the Jewish people.

family.title: Singing with his own
family.text: On stage and in the studio, the music is handed down. He often sings with his son, the Chassidic singer David Sitbon, and sometimes with his grandchildren.

son.title: The son, on stage
son.text: His son David Sitbon is a Chassidic singer in his own right: in 2025 he celebrates fifteen years on stage in Israel and abroad. During the war he sang at dozens of IDF bases, and he shared the stage with Mordechai Ben David in France (2011).

today.title: Today: his new songs
today.intro: Since his return in 2014 he has never stopped: he composes, he records, and a new song comes out almost every year.

guest.title: Invite him for a moment: chuppah, gala, wedding
guest.desc: Aharon Sitbon can come and sing a special moment at a wedding, a chuppah or a gala, alongside your band: one or two songs, his story, and a lot of emotion.
guest.h1: A moment of emotion, not a party set
guest.intro: Aharon Sitbon is not a party singer: he comes for a few songs and gives a moment people remember. Under the chuppah, in the middle of a gala, or when the room settles at the end of the evening.

audience.title: His audience – messages from all over the world
audience.desc: What listeners write to Aharon Sitbon under his videos: messages from Israel, France and Latin America, and more than 6 million views on YouTube.
audience.intro: In Hebrew, French, English, Spanish, Portuguese and even Russian, messages keep pouring in under his videos. From Mexico to Chile, from France to Israel, strangers write to tell him what his voice did for them. Here are a few, copied as written on YouTube.

home.latestText: A song about the miracle of Purim, released in March 2026, with a video by Zeevi Heller.
home.storyText: Gilbert Sitbon sang about love in French. One day in Paris, Chabad Chassidim offered him to put on tefillin. He left the stage at its height, studied for thirty years, then a melody kept him awake at night: Adon Olam.
home.ctaText: Listen to his albums, follow his channel, or send him a few words.
home.todayText: He keeps composing, and a new song comes out almost every year, made with Eli Klein and Yitzy Berry, often with his son David.
home.eventsText: The Olympia, Menorah Hall before thousands, the Tower of David, the Tzama convention: a voice that has filled halls, then and now.

spanish.title: Rey Mesías
spanish.subtitle: Melech HaMashiach · מלך המשיח
spanish.text: With its Spanish translation, “Melech HaMashiach” has travelled all over Latin America: more than 2.2 million views and over 1,000 comments on YouTube. In total, his songs have reached nearly 5 million views worldwide.
